description: Music royalty statement parser: 7 vendor formats to one tied-out dataset and Excel earnings tape. Rust → WebAssembly, runs in the browser at perpendis.com/royalty — files never leave the machine.

readme.text:
# nash-royalty-engine

A Rust engine that parses music royalty statements (DistroKid, TuneCore, CD Baby,
Symphonic, ASCAP, MLC, publisher CSVs) into one canonical line-item dataset,
proves the extraction with an exact-decimal **tie-out**, and writes the deliverable
a catalog-diligence buyer actually opens — a multi-sheet Excel **earnings tape**.
The same engine compiles to WebAssembly and runs live in the browser at
[perpendis.com/royalty](https://perpendis.com/royalty/), where statements are
parsed entirely client-side — **files never leave the machine**.

## Why it's interesting

- **Money is `rust_decimal::Decimal`, never `f64`.** Extracted rows must sum to
  the statement's reported totals within $0.01, or the statement is flagged
  BROKEN. A statement that reconciles by floating-point accident is worse than
  one that fails loudly.
- **Rows are never silently dropped or coerced.** An unparseable amount is a
  warning with a row number, never a zero. Unmapped source columns are preserved
  as JSON; every line carries the SHA-256 of its source file and its row number.
- **One engine, two targets.** The exact parser/tie-out/xlsx code that runs in
  the CLI is exported over a hand-rolled wasm ABI (no wasm-bindgen, no JS glue
  framework) and does all its work inside the browser tab.

## Results on real data

From [docs/FINDINGS.md](docs/FINDINGS.md) (Aug 2026, validation corpus of real
statements found in public sources — not redistributed here):

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Real + fixture rows parsed | **553,075** across 12 statements |
| Unparseable-amount warnings on real data | **0** (only the deliberately poisoned fixture warns, exactly on its poisoned cells) |
| Wrong-file rejections | 9/9 correct — registration and metadata tables refused, not hallucinated |
| Cross-parser validation | 200k-row file: generic parser and DMP parser agree to the cent ($10,010,176.22) |
| Full-corpus runtime (release build) | **9.6 seconds** (~150MB input) |

## Layout

```
crates/
  royalty-core/     canonical schema, encoding/delimiter sniffing, format
                    detection registry, exact-decimal tie-out validator
  royalty-parsers/  per-source parsers: header-fingerprint detection,
                    alias-tolerant column mapping, footer-total capture
  royalty-tape/     6-sheet Excel earnings-tape writer
  royalty-cli/      `nash` binary: inspect | run
  nash-wasm/        wasm export of the whole pipeline (raw ABI, no JS glue)
samples/
  synthetic/        synthetic fixtures (safe to redistribute)
  specs/            our own transcriptions of vendor format documentation,
                    with source URLs
vendor/
  rust_xlsxwriter/  vendored (MIT/Apache-2.0, licenses included) with one
                    local patch: system_now() returns a constant on plain
                    wasm32 instead of panicking (src/datetime.rs)
```

## Build & test

All commands below were run on a clean copy of this tree.

```
$ cargo test
test result: ok. 1 passed  (nash-wasm)
test result: ok. 3 passed  (royalty-core)
test result: ok. 7 passed  (royalty-parsers tests/parsers.rs)
# 11 tests, 0 failed
```

Build the wasm engine, then run the end-to-end ABI test in Node:

```
$ cargo build -p nash-wasm --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --profile wasm-release
    Finished `wasm-release` profile [optimized] target(s) in 25.48s
# -> target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/wasm-release/nash_wasm.wasm (~1.1 MB)

$ node scripts/test-wasm.mjs
add tsv rc: 0
add mlc tsv rc: 0
add zip rc: 0
statements: distrokid:7rows:1pg:self_consistent | mlc:4rows:1pg:self_consistent | distrokid:7rows:1pg:self_consistent | tunecore:4rows:1pg:self_consistent
failures: 0 total_net: 289.526501 pages: 4
csv rc: 0 bytes: 9233
xlsx rc: 0 bytes: 10898
WASM E2E: PASS
```

CLI use:

```
cargo run -p royalty-cli -- inspect <files...>
cargo run -p royalty-cli -- run <files-or-dirs...> --out out [--generic-fallback]
```

`run` writes `normalized.csv` (canonical line items with provenance),
`tieout.csv` (per-statement reconciliation ledger), `summary.json`, and
`tape.xlsx` (Summary, Tie-Out, By Period, By DSP, Top Tracks, Lines).

## Limitations (honest)

- **No PDF lane.** Label/PRO PDF statements are out of scope for the engine;
  that tail is a human-in-the-loop problem, not a parsing problem.
- ASCAP, MLC, TuneCore and Symphonic parsers were built against the vendors'
  own published format documentation (transcribed in `samples/specs/`) and
  spec-conformant fixtures — no genuine files for those formats exist publicly,
  so first real statements are the true test. The alias-table architecture is
  designed to absorb surprises.
- BMI CSV and SoundExchange detail-CSV have no public schema at all; both
  need a live account export.
- Single-currency assumption (USD) outside sources that carry a currency
  column; FX normalization is schema-ready but not wired.

## License

[PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](LICENSE.md) — source published for verification
of what the live tool does with your files; commercial use of the engine
requires a separate license. The vendored `rust_xlsxwriter` remains under its
own MIT/Apache-2.0 terms (see `vendor/rust_xlsxwriter/`).

Part of the [vbounds.com](https://vbounds.com) project line.
